A security release, plus three fixes from people trying it out. If you use usnfetch only on the
computer it runs on, without a web password, this one is mostly for you: upgrade.

**Upgrading:** replace `usnfetch.exe` and start it as usual. If you open usnfetch by a name other
than `localhost`, an IP address or the computer's own name (a hosts-file alias, a reverse proxy on
the same machine) and have no web password, set one first (Settings → Web access), or it will turn
that name away.

## Security

- **Other web pages can't use it.** Before, any page open in your browser could send usnfetch
  requests behind your back: queue downloads, change settings, reset everything. Now a change has
  to come from usnfetch's own page, and as JSON, which other sites can't send without asking first.
- **It answers only to this computer's names.** Without a web password, usnfetch answers to
  `localhost`, its IP addresses and the computer's own name. A website can no longer point a name
  of its own at your machine to get in (DNS rebinding). With a password, any name works as before.
- **A share's files can't run anything.** Every file from a share is served sandboxed, and web
  pages, SVGs opened in a tab and scripts show as plain text. Before, a web page inside a share
  opened in a new tab ran with usnfetch's own address, and could have used it as you.
- **A saved provider password goes only to its server.** Change a provider's server name and you
  type the password again, for Test connection too.
- **The 7-Zip and UnRAR paths** can only be changed on the computer running usnfetch, and only to
  7-Zip or UnRAR themselves.
- **Links in imported lists** are followed only when they're web pages (http or https).
- **Unpacking has limits.** A piece of a share's index read in one go can't unpack to more than
  1 GB, a packed article to more than 64 MB, and zstd data can't ask for more than a 128 MB window,
  all far past anything a real share uses.

## Fixes

- **A cut-off link is the share you already have.** Forums wrap long lines, and a link missing its
  last few characters used to count as a new share, so downloading it fetched the whole build
  again into a folder next to the first. Add links, Open link and Import now recognise it, and a
  `usenet://` link too, and use the link in your catalog. A link that says more than the one you
  have (the publisher's key, the folder key) is kept as it is.
- **Builds you downloaded without browsing are in Search** once the download is done, and their
  catalog row says what's in them. Ones downloaded before this are worked out in the background
  about 20 seconds after usnfetch starts.
- **Not enough room is a pause, not a failure.** With Keep free on (5 GB unless you change it), a
  download bigger than the free space starts anyway, pauses when the drive gets down to Keep free,
  and carries on once you make room. The review says so, and says when a size is only what the
  list claims. With Keep free off, it still fails as it starts.
